A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pri-TPG study despite retitling. Their complete 15-page contents, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original geometry-solving results on three benchmarks, alongside component ablations, retrieval analyses and backbone comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds GPT-5.2 ablations and prior-assisted classical-search experiments in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The proposed Pri-TPG retrieval, graph construction, symbolic filtering, candidate scoring and iterative inference remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A and C. The added classical-search combinations are experimental controls, without revision to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FormalGeo7K, Geometry3K and GeoQA under the same formal-input geometry tasks. Appendix B.2 varies backbones and search controls without adding datasets or task scenarios.

E2.justification: New Table 12 adds Prior + ForwardSearch and Prior + BackwardSearch as comparators alongside unassisted search and Pri-TPG. Comparator membership in the existing main benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 extends component ablations to GPT-5.2 and introduces classical-search controls. Table 2 also replaces the parsed-subset description with a 92%+ HyperGNet-aligned subset excluding duplicate diagrams; this revises the reported subset specification without establishing changed membership or rerun results.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 newly tests whether ablation trends persist with GPT-5.2 and whether retrieval priors benefit classical search without LLM planning. Existing feedback, structural-prior, retrieval and candidate-prioritization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added experiments retain point-accuracy reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 11 reports GPT-5.2 accuracies of 28.07% for ICL LLM and 63.43% for the query-adaptive prior. Table 12 adds 54.43% for Prior + ForwardSearch and 48.14% for Prior + BackwardSearch. These are newly reported variant results; existing benchmark scores, including Pri-TPG's 89.29%, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, graph and scoring definitions, equations (1)–(7), and mathematical reasoning are retained. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The structural-drift diagnosis, training-free structural-prior contribution and 89.29% performance claim are retained. The geometry-specific title and opening clarify the established task; the contribution list and conclusion retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 interprets classical-search gains primarily as action-space pruning and argues that LLMs better exploit richer TPG guidance. It also interprets the GPT-5.2 checks as supporting the smaller-model ablations. Section 4.2 adds potential integration with trained solvers; existing efficiency and long-proof limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code repository address and expands Table 2's subset and missing-comparison explanations. The explicit training-only retrieval assurance largely restates v1 Appendix A.1. Hyperparameters, scoring implementation details and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and Related Work section are unchanged. However, Section 4.2 adds positioning as a complementary search module for existing trained neural-symbolic solvers, extending the retained training-free alternative positioning.

P1.justification: Changes include retitling, localized abstract and introduction edits, affiliation and publication-header updates, acknowledgments, and a new Appendix B.2 subsection. Most prose and the overall section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 replaces a mismatched geometry diagram with one matching the problem statement. Table 5 displays Easy/Medium/Hard instead of Total/Easy/Medium, with totals retained in Table 9. Tables 11–12, expanded captions and limited table/prompt repositioning are added without substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: The new GPT-5.2 ablations and classical-search controls strengthen evidence about backbone dependence and the prior's contribution beyond the checks in v1. The code address, evaluation disclosures and corrected Figure 2 improve transparency and clarity. Gains are limited by sparse implementation details for the new controls, absent uncertainty reporting and untested claims about integration with trained solvers.
